transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46m
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Dana Kim (AvanTech - Procurement), Marcus Lee (AvanTech - Legal), Sofia Alvarez (AvanTech CTO), Ken Patel (AvanTech Infra), Tom Rhee (AvanTech Finance)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood Infrence, this is Priya our solutions eng, and Janelle who will be your CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Dana: Doing well, thanks. We kicked this off because procurement needs to lock terms and pricing before leadership signs off.
[00:12] Marcus: Hi. Legal will have a few redlines on the MSA and DPA so want to surface them early.
[00:17] Priya: Great — we'll walk through the typical enterprise terms and the onboarding flow, and then leave time for Q&A. Quick note, sorry if audio is a bit rough, I have a little background noise.
[00:28] Liam: First off, on the MSA/DPA — Redwood's standard MSA covers liability caps, data handling, subprocessor lists, and a standard DPA with EU addendum. We can share the PDFs after the call.
[00:38] Marcus: On liability caps: AvanTech needs reciprocity on IP carve-outs for customer data, and a clearer definition of "access" for debug. Also need to confirm retention windows.
[00:48] Liam: Totally. Our usual approach is to keep customer data out of model-training by default and commit to retention windows configurable per-customer. We do have SOC2 Type II and can provide the cert and pen-test summary.
[00:58] Dana: That's critical. Also, for regulated clients, we may need a VPC/on-prem option. How does Redwood handle private deployments and key management?
[01:08] Priya: We support Redwood Private — VPC peering or on-prem appliance. For keys, we integrate with KMS and optional HSM via common providers. Note: in some transcripts you'll see us say KV cashe — that's cache, sorry — we do prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost.
[01:25] Ken: If we go VPC, we need clear network egress expectations and whether Redwood requires peering or supports privatelink. Any networking docs?
[01:33] Janelle: We'll share a network diagram and peering playbook. For high-security customers we recommend private peering or provate link — sorry, privatelink — and we can walk through routing rules.
[01:45] Tom: Pricing — finance will need committed usage numbers and what discounts apply for reserved capacity. We need to know billing cadence and PO flow.
[01:53] Liam: Pricing has two main paths: hosted usage-based tiers (per-token plus embeddings) and Dedicated/reserved capacity with commit discounts. Typical billing is monthly; enterprise contracts can do quarterly or annual invoicing on PO. We can include a pricing spreadsheet.
[02:08] Sofia: For SLA, our product needs sub-100ms median tail latency for 2k context loads. Do you publish latency SLOs per model?
[02:16] Priya: We publish performance profiles per model — though tail latency depends on sequence length and batching. For Dedicated we can target tighter SLOs. We'll capture exact numbers in the SLA draft. Note: our runtime is optimized for continous batching and kernel selection but if you see notes about Redwod runtime in docs that's just a typo.
[02:34] Marcus: SLA credits — we will want specific remedies tied to revenue-impacting downtime, not just credits. Also audit rights for security incidents.
[02:43] Liam: Understandable. Our standard is service credits; for larger deals we've negotiated more specific remedies. We can escalate that with legal. Audit rights: we provide logging and access for security audits, and SOC2 plus on-site options for private deployments.
[02:57] Dana: DPA specifics: do you support EU data residency and subprocesser list disclosures?
[03:03] Liam: Yes, EU addendum available, and we provide subprocesser list. For residency we have region pinning for hosted; private gives full control.
[03:12] Ken: From an infra perspective, we want to run a small pilot: 2-3 routes, ~50 qps, and verify latency and cost at our typical prompt shapes. Priya, can you run the benchmark and share a short report?
[03:22] Priya: Absolutely. We'll test with your 8k-ish context samples, enable prefix/KV caching, and measure P50/P95/P99, plus tokens-per-request cost. Expect a short writeup.
[03:33] Marcus: On legal docs — what is your preferred redline flow? Word doc? DocuSign?
[03:39] Liam: We usually accept redlines in Word or markups in Google Docs; we can put the MSA and DPA into your redline environment. Final signing via DocuSign preferred.
[03:47] Tom: Need to confirm termination and notice periods — finance prefers 60 days for annual contracts.
[03:51] Liam: Our standard is 30-90 days depending on commitment; we can align on 60 in the draft.
[03:56] Dana: We're also concerned about data deletion after termination and portable export of logs.
[04:01] Priya: We can provide export of your transaction logs and confirm deletion procedures — we’ll document retention and deletion steps in the DPA.
[04:09] (crosstalk)
[04:15] Sofia: Are there any scaling guarantees if we spike? We need burst capacity for seasonal loads.
[04:20] Liam: For Hosted we have burst limits and scale policies; Dedicated offers configurable autoscaling with reserved capacity plus burst credit. We'll put those options in the ops annex.
[04:30] Ken: On encryption, do you support customer-managed keys for model inference payloads?
[04:34] Priya: Yes, CMKs via KMS, and HSM options for Private. There may be some tradeoffs around cache persistence with CMK — we'll document that.
[04:43] Marcus: Can you share pen test summary and any recent incident reports redacted?
[04:47] Janelle: We'll share SOC2 report, pen test high-level, and summary of incident response playbooks. Full reports appended under NDA if required.
[04:57] Liam: Ok, recap of next steps: we'll share MSA/DPA, pricing sheet, SOC2/pen test summary, and a network diagram. Priya will run the benchmark. Marcus to return legal redlines. We schedule onboarding tech deep-dive for Sep 1 tentatively.
[05:12] Dana: That works. One more ask: can you include sample SLA language referencing specific P99 latency thresholds and objective measurement windows?
[05:20] Priya: Yes, we'll draft suggested SLA clauses including P50/P95/P99 windows and the measurement method, plus remedies.
[05:28] Tom: On invoicing, can Redwood accept master PO with monthly invoices?
[05:31] Liam: Yes, that is standard. We'll align payment terms in the MSA appendix.
[05:37] (brief pause)
[05:40] Marcus: A couple of typos I noted in the sample security docs where k/v cache is spelled KV cashe — minor but want clean deliverables.
[05:46] Priya: Thanks, we'll clean up docs.
[05:50] Liam: Any last blockers?
[05:53] Sofia: Technical team wants to review the TLS cipher suites and private link options; Ken will follow up with network diagrams.
[05:59] Ken: Yep, will send diagrams by Friday.
[06:02] Liam: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll send the docs and set up the deep-dive.
[06:06] Dana: Thanks.
[06:07] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some words mis-transcribed (Redwood spelled as Redwod, KV cashe, privatelink/privatelink written inconsistently). Timestamps approximate.
